reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an official rap music release centered on the song "Boht Tej," its performers, and a stylized performance video. The references to listening or downloading through named music services, including the Wynk Music prompt, are consistent with ordinary song access and distribution rather than financial participation. The described material does not establish deceptive claims or a financial mechanism.

opening.argument: Judge the call to action, not just the performance. The description offers access to a digital song and immediately tells viewers where to obtain it: “Listen & Download Boht Tej,” followed by a JioSaavn song link. It also directs Jio users to download an app to set the track as a Jio Tune. That is a concrete acquisition pathway, even though the surrounding material presents it as entertainment. The evidence does not establish what a viewer encounters after following either instruction, so the music-video framing alone should not settle the question of those flows.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The song title, artist credits, and Delhi-themed description establish what is being promoted, but they do not establish what happens when a viewer follows the download instructions. The defense treats named music services as dispositive. The description nevertheless asks viewers to take an action outside the video to obtain the track, and the Jio Tune instruction adds an app-download step. Those steps deserve scrutiny on their own terms.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An acquisition pathway is not, by itself, a deceptive reward offer. The stated object is the named song, and the description identifies its artists and music credits. The cited instructions promise only listening, downloading, or setting that song as a Jio Tune. They do not claim a free or unusually easy reward, conceal a different asset, or describe a misleading verification flow.

opening.argument: The description places numerous outbound access points beside the invitation to listen and download, including links for JioSaavn, Wynk, Gaana, and Spotify. It also gives carrier-specific dialing instructions for setting the track as a caller tune. A viewer is being steered among several services and phone-based actions, not merely shown a performance. The supplied material does not verify the destination experience or explain any terms attached to those actions. That gap matters when assessing whether the apparent offer of easy song access is as straightforward as it sounds.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the named services are consistent with ordinary distribution. Consistency is not verification: the cited description also asks some viewers to dial numbers to set a caller tune, while others are directed to an app. The music credits explain the video’s presentation but do not establish the terms or outcome of each requested action. The judge should assess that promotional pathway as well as the song itself.

citations.quote: To set "Boht Tej" as your caller tune: Airtel subscribers Dial 5432117406181 Vodafone subscribers Dial 53711958695
Jio users, download the JioSavan Music App to set this song as your Jio Tune

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Multiple music links and carrier-specific caller-tune instructions are ordinary ways to distribute a song. Nothing cited promises cash, a free asset, or a reward beyond access to the identified track; nor does an absence of downstream verification establish deception. The description expressly identifies the song and performers, making the purpose of the links clear.

opening.argument: This is not only a performance presented for passive viewing. Its description turns the song into a series of participation prompts: listen and download it through linked services, dial to set it as a caller tune, or download an app to make it a Jio Tune. The visible Wynk Music prompt reinforces the same direction to leave the performance and obtain the track. The entertainment presentation gives those prompts a familiar context, but it should not prevent the judge from examining the requested actions as part of the offer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s description of a rap release is accurate but incomplete. Its own cited access instructions show that viewers are also asked to act: follow a music link or download an app to set a tune. Those prompts are part of the content’s purpose, not incidental background. Artist credits and a song title do not answer every question about what the viewer is being asked to do.

citations.quote: Listen & Download Boht Tej : JioSaavn : https://www.jiosaavn.com/song/boht-tej/PB0ydSd-aEo

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is not the same as a scam. The requested actions are specifically tied to listening to the identified song or setting it as a caller tune. The opening identifies no separate reward, deceptive promise, or concealed participation requirement. The performance and the promotional instructions therefore support the same ordinary music-release reading.
